risks.title: Increased competition from cloud vendors
risks.score_rationale: The risk is central in the 10-K, mentioned at the outset of the risk factors. The language is strong ("materially affect", "reduction in sales"). It reflects an upward structural trend driven by cloud adoption. The Competition category is highly weighted here.

risks.title: Loss of partner funding
risks.score_rationale: The section on 'partner funding' is lengthy and detailed, with mention of material impacts on results. The risk involves major partners (Microsoft, Cisco, etc.). The tone is concerned, with references to recent impacts. The Capital category is heavily affected.

risks.title: Obsolescence of hardware inventory
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of past write-downs on hardware. The risk is recurring and tied to accelerating technological change. The language is firm ("write-downs", "no return privileges"). The Industrial category has medium weight.

risks.title: Dependence on key partners
risks.score_rationale: Absence of long-term contracts with critical partners (Microsoft, Cisco, Ingram Micro). Risk of disruption is explicit, with potential for operational impact. The language is alarming ("could negatively impact"). The Competition category is critical.

risks.title: Pricing and margin pressures
risks.score_rationale: The pricing factor is mentioned multiple times, with reference to persistent pressures. The language is strong ("very aggressive", "reduced operating margins"). Direct impact on profitability. The Competition category is dominant.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks in Europe
risks.score_rationale: Specific mention of conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, with effects on European operations. The language is concerned ("market disruptions", "supply chain disruptions"). The Geopolitical category is moderately weighted but rising.

risks.title: Changes in IT purchasing decisions
risks.score_rationale: Risk related to decentralization of IT procurement toward end users. Explicit mention of potential material impact. The language is clear and preventive. The Industrial category is relevant.

ai_positioning.summary: NSIT does not mention artificial intelligence in its 10-K/20-F filing.
